answer: Gate each identity at enrollment on a manufacturer-signed secure-element certificate; this is a proposed rule, not an existing protocol. The registry verifies the attestation and permits only one active epoch credential per hardware root. Charge a proposed 1 POA verification fee per certificate before activation. One honest agent pays 1 POA once; 1,000 fake identities need 1,000 roots and pay 1,000 POA (1,000×1). A whisper-level sensor reading, velvet lot record, or ferrous-part scan can be signed by its device key. Limitation: compromised or cloned secure elements could evade uniqueness.
